epic.intent:
Replace Bannerlord's human appearance system and creator with equivalent customization controls and visual quality to Dragon's Dogma 2, using an original Bannerlord-fitting asset catalog. User confirmed all human characters including troops, and original catalog rather than copying DD2's complete selection catalog. Cover player, nobles, companions, civilians, bandits, troops, all native male/female maturity definitions and adult aging. Improvements must appear in actual gameplay, equipment and portraits as well as the creator. This is a vetted future implementation plan, not implemented or runtime-verified functionality.

Study DD2's complete human creator controls and observable behavior, then build and validate Bannerlord-native or explicitly proven extended mechanisms. Keep full control/quality parity as the outcome; unsupported capabilities are unmet requirements, not permission to silently narrow the result. Original asset production is required work, including modeling, deformation, material/texture authoring, hair and necessary equipment corrections. No assumption that an imported static model, one added slider, XML references, or code generation alone delivers the requested result.

Installed-file evidence establishes Bannerlord v1.4.8, shared human heads across ten skin definitions, 63 declared deform keys per skin, a 512-bit static appearance container, a 320-entry marshalled weight array and native FaceGen calls; none of these establishes extension capacity. DD2 and REFramework are installed, but complete creator mapping and fresh runtime/toolchain validation remain required. Scope and product decisions will be frozen before dependent production, with no unsupported feature marked complete. Execution is not requested now; save in Backlog and start no run.

Original catalog assets meet the frozen breadth and quality specification; required blocked entries prevent completion.

Original male/female heads, bodies, eyes, mouth, hair, facial hair, skin and markings meet the frozen DD2 reference-quality rubric in creator and gameplay lighting, with functioning facial animation, complete detail levels, valid seams and no unacceptable deformation artifacts.

All human categories and all ten native sex/maturity skin definitions use the production system in gameplay, portraits and menus; aging, maturation, inheritance and population generation retain valid identities and varied appearances.

All equipment in the frozen supported native/installed-DLC roster has a verified compatibility disposition for required body/head controls, gender/coverage/detail variants and combat/mounted poses; required unresolved refits, clipping, reach or collision defects remain failures.

Creator controls, reset/undo, presets and portable appearance import/export operate on the real schema. Hero appearance and documented troop seed semantics survive applicable mission/campaign lifecycles, cold save/load and version migration without ID drift, cross-character state leakage or silent face regeneration.

The complete mixed human population passes repeatable battle, siege, town, dialogue and portrait benchmarks on the pinned target within numeric frame-time, memory and loading budgets frozen before production; detail transitions preserve valid appearance and silhouettes.

A reproducible version-pinned local package passes independent full option, asset, equipment, maturity, persistence and visual acceptance audits; the final human review receives actual gameplay evidence. Technical probes, incomplete catalogs, unsupported mechanisms or unrun tests cannot satisfy the finished outcome.

bundle.rationale:
User-confirmed outcome: DD2-equivalent human customization controls and visual quality with an original Bannerlord-fitting asset catalog, for every human including troops. Planning only; this backlog does not assert runtime feasibility has passed. The single-player/multiplayer clarification is pending until the user's answer is recorded; dependent scope is not guessed.

Why three milestones: technical capability/contract work must precede production. The actual original catalog and armor workload cannot honestly be enumerated before inspection. During milestone 1, the planner expands the FUTURE production sprint into exact-ID medium-or-smaller batches, wires all required batches into family closure and acceptance coverage, validates/saves, and the orchestrator adopts that revision at the checkpoint. This obeys the server rule against editing an active/passed sprint and avoids dispatching broad art families as pretend bounded tasks. Milestone 2 delivers the complete system; milestone 3 provides independent finished-product validation. These are dependency milestones, not calendar duration estimates. Default human checkpoints remain server-controlled; no checkpoint or run is approved/started by this planning task.

Parallelism: after setup, reference capture, baseline measurement, equipment inventory and head/native-channel investigation can prepare independently. Shared app/editor work remains single-owner and queued. Reference mapping and the head probe join for capacity tests; material/body probes and wardrobe inspection join into the contract. Runtime services and source-art preparation proceed independently after the accepted contract/import pipeline. Production catalog integration genuinely combines their bindings for downstream wardrobe closure and optimization. Final visual, lifecycle and compatibility audits can prepare in parallel, serializing live runtime checks; packaging waits for all three.

Critical path is determined by measurements, not a guessed duration: setup -> reference/native probes -> full mechanism and clothed-body proof -> contract/batch expansion -> runtime/import pipeline -> complete original body/head/maturity/hair/equipment catalog -> combined catalog/wardrobe -> performance -> independent audits -> package. There is no dependency on completion of the sibling combat, world or creature epics. Inspect their stable identity, rig/animation and human-only boundaries; certify combined integration only against actual available builds.

Vetting findings incorporated: one added slider is only a probe, not full capacity; all 63 native declarations include bone/system semantics and require corpus sweeps; 320 marshalled weights and 512 packed bits imply no proven spare capacity. DD2 blend-shape import is not a dependable ready-made route. Original asset authoring and capable DCC operators are actual prerequisites. Skin/eye/hair rendering and clothed body deformation are early gates. All ten human sex/maturity definitions plus adult aging need production evidence. Complete item/variant wardrobe closure is separate from representative strategy tests. Stable IDs, nondestructive hero migration, explicit anonymous troop seed semantics, full render contexts and cache/material isolation are required. Soft/rigid family closure has a separate combined validation owner to avoid hidden circular waits.

Product decisions assigned to the capability contract: exact supported mode, pinned official module roster/version, original catalog breadth, observed voice/posture/gameplay-related control applicability, target battle load/settings and numeric budget, identity preservation and old-save/removal/downgrade policy, collision/reach effects, and troop seed lifetime. Resolve required ambiguous user choices before dependent production; no unrequested scope reduction or fabricated performance threshold. Use native-compatible identities/rig interfaces where proven, not as assumptions. Required failed mechanisms block their dependent work while independent work continues.

Project-wide Definition of Done is currently empty and was not changed for unrelated epics. Milestone acceptance reads its current value at execution and also applies the epic-specific covering criteria. Capability profiles are provider-neutral with minimal tools and image modality for actual visual work; no named model override or budget has been invented. No feature branch was created during planning because the user did not name one; execution setup chooses and records a codex/ feature branch before implementation and never merges directly to main. Remaining workload estimates follow measured inventory and capability results.


Final review corrections: full composition testing waits for material and clothed-body probes; aging tests wait for rendering-context adapters; baseline includes installed naval scenarios. Pre-contract wardrobe records use provisional diagnostic classifications, final mixed-outfit validation has one owner, and early maturity fits use accepted diagnostic attachments to avoid circular production dependencies. Future-production expansion covers engine/shader/tool/network work as well as art. The transitive dependency reduction preserves readiness while keeping the graph readable.
